hypotheses.justification: `hx` follows from `hfd` and `ht`. `Transcendental K x` is defined as `¬IsAlgebraic K x`, so argue by contradiction and suppose `IsAlgebraic K x`. Over a field this gives `IsIntegral K x` (`IsAlgebraic.isIntegral`). Then `IntermediateField.adjoin.finiteDimensional` (Mathlib, IntermediateField/Adjoin/Basic.lean:486) gives `FiniteDimensional K K⟮x⟯`. Together with `hfd : FiniteDimensional K⟮x⟯ F`, `Module.Finite.trans` (RingTheory/Finiteness/Basic.lean:365) gives `FiniteDimensional K F`; the needed scalar tower K → K⟮x⟯ → F is a standard instance. So F is algebraic over K (`Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_finite`), hence `t` is algebraic over K, which contradicts `ht`. With `hx` recovered this way at the start of the proof, the existing proof goes through unchanged, so the theorem stays true and provable without `hx`. No degenerate case gets in the way: whenever `x` is algebraic, the other hypotheses already contradict each other.
